newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ABB orders may hit $40 billion in '97-company head.
newsitem.headline: ABB orders may hit $40 billion in '97-company head.

text.p: The new head of Swedish-Swiss engineering giant ABB was quoted on Sunday as saying new orders could hit $40 billion for full year 1997.

Goran Lindahl, who has replaced Percy Barnevik as chief executive, told the Svenska Dagbladet daily that most growth was coming from immature markets in Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Eastern Europe.
"It might be $40 billion for the whole year provided we can keep the momentum going. But it might be 37 or 38 billion," Lindahl was quoted as saying.
ABB posted first quarter new orders of $10 billion.
The company has set a target of six percent turnover growth every year to achieve $50 billion turnover by the end of the century, the daily quoted Lindahl as saying.
